svg.title: Fabric Implementation Delivery Chain — Environments to Operational Readiness
svg.desc: A five-phase horizontal delivery chain. Dev, Test, and Production workspace environments feed Fabric deployment pipelines, which promote items and inject environment-specific configuration through Variable Libraries behind a pull-request gate. Promoted items then pass through a testing phase that validates data quality and, for mirrored items, must manually trigger replication because promotion alone leaves the target item empty. A security phase applies workspace and tenant-level access controls, with a warning that Deployment Pipelines and Fabric SQL Database stop working entirely if public access is blocked at the workspace or private links are enabled tenant-wide. The chain ends at operational readiness, where Item Recovery's up-to-90-day retention window and monitoring evidence gate whether the release is accepted. A feedback edge routes failed acceptance back to the environments phase.
svg.text: Reference phases for taking a change from a workspace environment to an operationally accepted Production release.

g.aria-label: Workspace environments: Dev, Test, and Production
g.title: Workspace environments (Dev / Test / Production) — Three workspaces form the promotion chain that deployment pipelines move items across; each stage has its own capacity, permissions, and connections.
g.text: Distinct workspace per stage, each on
its own capacity and role assignment,

g.aria-label: Deployment Pipelines: promote items with Variable Libraries and a pull-request gate
g.title: Deployment Pipelines — promote + Variable Libraries — Deployment Pipelines promotes items across Dev, Test, and Production while Variable Libraries swap in environment-specific connection strings, gated by a pull request.

g.text: swap connection strings per stage so
one item definition targets many envs.

g.aria-label: Testing: quality gates and the mirroring replication trigger
g.title: Testing — quality gates + mirroring replication trigger — Promoted items are validated for quality before serving; any mirrored database item needs its replication triggered manually since promotion alone leaves it empty.

g.aria-label: Security: workspace and tenant access controls, warning on Deployment Pipelines being disabled
g.title: Security — workspace and tenant access controls — Workspace-level Block Public Access and tenant-level private links are real architectural trade-offs: both disable Deployment Pipelines and Fabric SQL Database outright, not just restrict them.

svg.text: branch: Block Public Access / tenant private links disable Deployment Pipelines outright

g.aria-label: Operational readiness: Item Recovery retention and monitoring gate
g.title: Operational readiness — Item Recovery + monitoring gate — Release is accepted only once monitoring evidence exists and the Item Recovery retention window is confirmed as the safety net for the newly promoted items.

svg.text: feedback: failed acceptance sends the release back to Dev
OneLake — the shared substrate under every phase
Every workspace, every promoted item, and every mirrored replica read and write the same Delta tables across all five phases.
